newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Higher pork prices push up Dutch inflation rate.
newsitem.headline: Higher pork prices push up Dutch inflation rate.

text.p: Higher prices for food and for pork in particular drove up the Dutch consumer price index in May, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said.
The Dutch May CPI rose 0.3 percent compared with April and was up 2.2 percent compared with May 1996.
Both figures were higher than economists' consensus estimates of zero and 1.9 percent respectively.
The month-on-month rise was largely driven by a one percent rise in the food and drink sub-index, which in turn included a 2.8 percent rise in the meat component.
The CBS said wholesale pork prices had risen sharply in the first quarter of this year as a result of a continuing swine fever epidemic which has reduced the supply of pork.
In May, the increased wholesale prices were partially passed on to consumers who had to pay an average of 10 percent more for pork in shops compared with preceding months.
The CBS noted that coffee prices had also risen sharply recently as a result of poor harvests and a stronger dollar.
In May, consumers paid some 20 percent more for a pack of coffee than they did in January.
The coffee, tea and cocoa component of the food CPI subindex rose 3.8 percent between April and May but it has a weighting of only 5/1000 in the CPI compared with 38/1000 for meat.
